text:
alex: Quick design review — I'm prototyping a compact 'version replay' panel for the rollouts page. Figma: https://www.figma.com/file/abcd1234/version-replay-compact (link) :eyes: maya: Nice. What's the main goal? reduce vertical space on the timeline? or help debugging rollback reasons? alex: Both. Idea: small timeline strip + an inline diff/replay pane that expands. Keeps history dense for teams with many micro-rollouts. sam: Pixel nit: the timeline dots are pretty tight at 1200px. Maybe increase hit target. Also the hover state needs keyboard focus equivalent. patrick: a11y check: color contrast on the 'replay' chips is borderline. Also need aria-live when the replay pane opens so screen readers announce context. maya: Good call. Proposed microcopy for the replay CTA: `Open version replay — shows changes between selected rollouts and lets you step through traffic splits.` Thoughts? alex: I like that. Shorten to: `Open version replay — step through diffs & traffic.` Less copy in the UI. patrick: For aria, suggest this snippet:```html
...
``` Make sure focus moves into the panel on open and returns on close. maya: Also thinking about the rollback confirm flow. Current modal says "Rollback to version X". Could we add a small line: "This will send 100% traffic to version X unless you choose a canary." sam: UX question: Should rollback default to immediate 100% or to a staged canary (like 10% for 10 minutes)? Platform teams want safe defaults. alex: We're leaning towards staged by default for safety, with a clear dropdown to set allocation & duration. The primary action will say "Rollback (staged)" with a link to advanced options. maya: Visual for the allocation slider: add tick marks at common breakpoints: 1%, 5%, 10%, 25%, 50%, 100%. Also show a live throughput estimate under the slider (tokens/sec) so engineers can see cost/latency impact. patrick: Slider needs keyboard support: arrow keys adjust by small increments, PageUp/PageDown jump by larger ones, Home/End to min/max. Provide aria-valuetext e.g. `10 percent, approx 1.2k req/min`. sam: Implementation note: we'll need a compact token to render the timeline markers; I'm thinking an SVG strip with accessible labels. I'll prototype. maya: Microcopy nit: When a canary is active, copy should say `Canary (X% for Y min)` and the status dot should have a tooltip: `Traffic allocation: X% — created by at `. alex: API/model question: Do we store snapshots for every rollout? We discussed lightweight diffs vs full snapshot. Preference is diffs to save storage but show a replay as if full snapshot exists. sam: Backend: we can reconstruct state by applying diffs sequentially. Frontend needs a compact timeline index for quick seeks. We'll add a `snapshot_index` endpoint. patrick: Accessibility acceptance test suggestions: 1) Keyboard only: open replay, step through diffs, and close. 2) Screen reader: verify announcements at open/close and when the allocation slider changes. 3) High contrast mode: colors meet 4.5:1. maya: One more design question — history density. If there are >20 rollouts in last 24h, we compress to a condensed mode that groups minor micro-rollouts (same author + <1% traffic) behind a chevron. Expandable. Thoughts? alex: Yes — plus a legend pill: `20 events shown • 5 collapsed`. Users can toggle `Show all` in settings. sam: I'll add a tiny keyboard shortcut: `g r` to jump to the Replay panel from the rollouts list. Need to ensure it doesn't conflict with other shortcuts. maya: For testing copy: small A/B test ideas — variant A: explicit "Staged rollback (recommended)" vs variant B: "Rollback (staged)" — measure confirmations and aborts. patrick: Agree. Also measure how often folks manually toggle to 100% immediately. If rare, keep staged as default. alex: Action items: @maya prototype updated Figma with keyboard & tooltip states (due tomorrow). @sam prototype minimal SVG timeline + keyboard interactions (PR next week). @patrick write a11y test checklist and aria copy. I'll set up an experiment in product to track the rollback defaults. aria-bot: Reminder: Accessibility review scheduled Fri 3pm. Add checklist items to the PR description. maya: Thanks — will update and ping here when ready :thumbsup: sam: I'll spin up a demo branch and link it here when available. alex: Great work team — keeping this compact will help support heavy-traffic orgs. :shipit:
